concepts.def: Smallest meaningful unit of sound; English has around 44 phonemes; minimal pairs (pat/bat) distinguish them.
International Phonetic Alphabet; standardised notation for all human speech sounds; UK uses Received Pronunciation /riˈsiːvd/.
How airflow is shaped: plosive (p,b), fricative (f,v), nasal (m,n), affricate (ch,j), approximant (w,y).
Where sound is made: bilabial (m), labiodental (f), alveolar (t), velar (k), glottal (h).
Vocal cord vibration distinguishes voiced (b,d,g,v,z) from voiceless (p,t,k,f,s) pairs.
Rhythm, stress and intonation patterns; pitch movement (rising for questions); supports meaning beyond words.

concepts.def: Smallest meaningful unit; 'cats' = cat + -s; differs from phoneme (sound) and word.
Free morphemes stand alone (cat); bound only attach (un-, -ing, -ed); affixes are bound.
Adding prefix (un-, re-) or suffix (-able, -ness); changes meaning or word class.
Inflection adds grammar (walked, books); derivation creates new word (happy to happiness, noun).
Combining two free morphemes: bookshelf, mother-in-law, blackbird; very productive in English.
Word changes class without affix; 'google' verb from noun; 'text' verb in mobile age.

Chomskyan generative syntax; all phrases share structure: specifier, head, complement; universal grammar.

concepts.def: Denotation = literal meaning ('home' = dwelling); connotation = associations (warmth, safety, family).
Set of words sharing meaning domain; e.g. football: pitch, goal, referee, foul, striker.
Synonyms similar (big/large); antonyms opposite: gradable (hot/cold), complementary (alive/dead), converse (buy/sell).
Word's meaning included in another's: dog is hyponym of animal (hypernym); poodle hyponym of dog.
Polysemy = one word multiple related meanings (bank of river vs financial); homonyms unrelated (bat animal/sport).
Pejoration (cunning once meant knowing), amelioration, broadening (dog from breed to species), narrowing.
